name: CLOPS (Circuit Layer Operations Per Second)
description: CLOPS is a hardware-agnostic speed metric developed by IBM that measures how fast a quantum processor can execute parameterized circuit layers. It captures the full hardware-software stack including gate execution speed, classical compilation time, control instruction generation, and data transfer rates. IBM updated the metric in 2023 to CLOPSh, replacing Quantum Volume with layer fidelity for a more comprehensive assessment.
significance: Industry-standard speed metric capturing full hardware-software stack performance, essential for comparing quantum processor throughput across platforms.

news.title: Quality, Speed, and Scale: three key attributes to measure the performance of near-term quantum computers
news.excerpt: We propose a speed benchmark, using an update to the quantum volume experiments that allows the measurement of Circuit Layer Operations Per Second (CLOPS) and identify how both classical and quantum components play a role in improving performance.

news.title: IBM Proposes Circuit Layer Operations Per Second (CLOPS) as Quantum Speed Metric
news.excerpt: IBM scientists propose CLOPS, a hardware-agnostic metric measuring how fast a quantum processor can execute parameterized circuit layers. The metric captures the full hardware-software stack including gate execution speed, runtime compilation, classical control instruction generation, and data transfer rates.

news.title: IBM Proposes a New Way to Measure Quantum Speed: CLOPS
news.excerpt: IBM researchers report a new quantum metric called Circuit Layer Operations Per Second (CLOPS) that measures the speed a quantum processor can execute layers of parameterized circuits. The fastest IBM systems can run up to 1,400 circuit layer operations per second.

news.title: QUOPS Rate (Ω) Proposed as Architecture-Agnostic Successor to CLOPS-Style Throughput Metrics
news.excerpt: The QUOPS paper from Sandia, Quantinuum, and NVIDIA introduces two complementary metrics: Q (maximum circuit size executed successfully) and Ω (QUOPS per second, a throughput rate). QUOPS rate directly parallels CLOPS as a cross-platform throughput benchmark but incorporates logical-qubit performance. Helios-1 reached 303 Ω/s, Willow 4,400 Ω/s, and ibm_boston 2,900 Ω/s — showing IBM and Google lead on speed while Quantinuum leads on circuit size.

news.title: Quantum Computers Need 100,000-Fold Performance Gain For Scientific Utility, Study Finds
news.excerpt: Benchmarking study by Sandia, Quantinuum, NVIDIA and partner labs introduces QUOPS as a cross-platform metric. The QUOPS rate (Ω, operations per second) parallels CLOPS as a throughput benchmark; the study benchmarks Google Willow (4,400 Ω/s), IBM ibm_boston (2,900 Ω/s), and Quantinuum Helios-1 (303 Ω/s) simultaneously — the first direct cross-platform throughput comparison of this scale.
